The expectation value of \(S_y\) is found by normalizing the state and computing \(\langle S_y \rangle = \frac{\langle \psi | S_y | \psi \rangle}{\langle \psi | \psi \rangle}\).

The state is \(|\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} 3i \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\), with norm squared \(\langle \psi | \psi \rangle = |3i|^2 + |4|^2 = 9 + 16 = 25\).

The spin operator is \(S_y = \frac{\hbar}{2} \sigma_y = \frac{\hbar}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix}\).

Compute \(\sigma_y |\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3i \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4i \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}\).

Then \(\langle \psi | \sigma_y | \psi \rangle = \begin{pmatrix} -3i & 4 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} -4i \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} = (-3i)(-4i) + 4(-3) = 12i^2 - 12 = -24\).

Thus \(\langle \psi | S_y | \psi \rangle = \frac{\hbar}{2}(-24) = -12\hbar\).

Finally, \(\langle S_y \rangle = \frac{-12\hbar}{25} = -\frac{12}{25}\hbar\).

Answer: C
